minutes.headline: Open Space Committee, lacking a quorum, took no vote on a Chapter 61B Leominster Road parcel and will ask for an appraisal.
minutes.summary: With only three members present, the committee discussed a Chapter 61B withdrawal notice on a Leominster Road wetland parcel and the town's right of first refusal. Members disagreed on whether to pursue it. It also reviewed site visits to the Lake Shirley parcels (Stump Cove and Parmenter Road), the town master plan kickoff, a trails grant award, and the meeting schedule. The chair will send a note to the town administrator asking for an appraisal, framed as a discussion and not a committee recommendation.

Decision deferred to the next monthly meeting; the town has about 120 days from the May notice, running into August.
The chair's note to the administrator will also ask her to follow up with town counsel on the title issue for the Reservoir Road parcel.
Next meetings set for July 12 and August 9; one member will be away August 9.
Reorganization of officers and a possible chair change will go on a future agenda.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee met without a quorum and took no vote on a Chapter 61B withdrawal notice for a Leominster Road parcel.
The chair will send the town administrator a note asking about an appraisal, framed as a discussion and not a committee recommendation.
The town's decision on its right of first refusal is deferred to the next monthly meeting; the window runs into August.
Members reviewed site visits to the Lake Shirley parcels; the chair's note will also ask the administrator to follow up with town counsel on a title question.
A trails grant was announced for engineering of parking and viewing access, with a local match required; next meetings were set for July 12 and August 9.

why_it_matters: Whether the town uses its right of first refusal on Chapter 61B land is decided on a clock, and a committee without a quorum cannot authorize even a small appraisal paid from the donated open space fund.
The trails grant carries a required local match, which would be a cost to the town if the project proceeds.
